Backup and restore

On this page
  • What a backup holds
  • Make a backup
  • Restore from a backup
  • The device's own backup

"Save your settings and your own sounds to a file you keep, to bring them back after clearing the app's data or on a new device."

What a backup holds

In the backup fileNot in the backup file
All your settings, including the current place and the favouritesThe offline map areas (download them again)
Your alert choicesThe street data kept for the mosques and directions
The mosques you added
Your own sounds (except in the web version)

The file is named after the day it was made, for example taqwim-backup-2026-11-06.json.

Make a backup

  1. Open Settings → General.
  2. Under Backup, tap Back up settings.
  3. Where the file goes depends on the device:
    • Android, iPhone and iPad: the system's save dialog opens; choose a place, such as a cloud drive or a folder.
    • Windows, macOS and Linux: the file is saved straight into your Downloads folder. If a file of that name exists, Taqwim adds a number.
    • Web: the browser downloads the file. "A backup from the browser holds no sounds."
  4. Taqwim confirms with Backup saved: and the file's name or place.

Restore from a backup

  1. Open Settings → General.
  2. Tap Restore from a backup and choose the backup file.
  3. Taqwim shows "This backup will replace all your current settings." and Made on: with the backup's date.
  4. Tap Restore from a backup again to confirm, or Cancel.
  5. Taqwim confirms: "Your settings were restored from the backup."

After a restore, the alerts are set again from the restored settings. Your own sounds are replaced by those in the backup; sounds that are not in the backup are removed.

If the restore fails

MessageMeaning
This file is not a Taqwim backup.Choose the .json file Taqwim made.
This backup comes from a newer Taqwim; update the app first.Install the latest version, then restore.
The file is too large to be a backup.The chosen file is not a backup.
The backup could not be read: …The file is damaged; the message gives the reason.

The device's own backup

Your phone's own backup can also keep Taqwim's settings in your account, if you have it turned on: Google's backup on Android, and iCloud or computer backups on iPhone and iPad. You control this in your device's settings. The offline map areas are left out of these backups.

A backup file contains your saved places. Keep it somewhere private.
